raw.query: WITH vllm AS (SELECT num_images AS N, mean_ms_per_image AS ms_per_img FROM provenance.v_vllm_vision_cost_by_n WHERE run_id='measured:vllm_h100_trace'), vd AS (SELECT N, ms_per_img, ms_per_img - lag(ms_per_img) OVER (ORDER BY N) AS d_ms FROM vllm) SELECT N, round(ms_per_img::numeric,3) ms_per_img, round(d_ms::numeric,3) d_ms FROM vd ORDER BY N; -- and batch_size invariance from provenance.encoder_factoring_probe WHERE image_px=448
raw.observed: vLLM ms/img: N=1 14.417, N=2 14.040 (-2.6%), N=4 13.867 (-3.8% cumulative), N=6 13.844, N=8 13.787 (-4.4% total); 86% of the 4.4% benefit is captured by N=4, ΔN=4→8 sums to +0.080ms (−0.6%, within N=4 noise). AIC encoder_factoring_probe at 448px: predicted_ms = 316.369 for batch_size=1,2,4,8,16,32,64 with total_images=64 -- i.e., AIC is strictly batch-invariant (Δ=0 by construction).
raw.evidence: Saturation point mis-located: vLLM gain curve flattens by N≈4, not N≈6–8; AIC shows 0 batching benefit at all (factoring invariance), not 'saturation by 6–8'.
